# Implementation Plan: Prompt Cache Optimization

**Branch**: `001-prompt-cache-optimization` | **Date**: 2026-07-11 | **Spec**: [spec.md](spec.md)

**Input**: Feature specification from `specs/001-prompt-cache-optimization/spec.md`

**Note**: Generated by `/speckit-plan`. Phase 0 output: [research.md](research.md). Phase 1
outputs: [data-model.md](data-model.md), [contracts/](contracts/), [quickstart.md](quickstart.md).

## Summary

MuhiyaCode's DeepSeek prefix-cache hit rate is too low because a handful of identified
mechanisms rewrite previously transmitted request bytes: MCP tools register asynchronously and
in nondeterministic order after the first request (and `/mcp` actions rebuild the block
mid-session), the system prompt embeds a build-time date, history maintenance rewrites settled
bytes too early and too often (fold at 0.55 pressure, per-turn trims above 0.65 driven by a
`len/4` estimate), and the web-search probe flaps across builds. Meanwhile cache accounting
collapses hit/miss into one field, ignores `prompt_cache_miss_tokens`, and loses cumulative
usage on resume — so none of this was visible or provable.

The fix, grounded in the DeepSeek Reasonix reference analysis ([research.md](research.md) Parts
A/C): pin a deterministic tool surface for the whole session from a persisted MCP schema cache;
move the date to the per-task brief; persist the web-probe snapshot; consolidate history
rewrites into rare, boundary-scheduled maintenance passes above a 0.60 pressure floor with an
anti-thrash latch and exact provider-token pressure inputs; strip reasoning replay to the
provider-required minimum; extend usage accounting to distinct, nullable cache-read/miss
fields persisted per session; hash the prefix shape per request so every miss is attributed to
a recorded invalidation event or the provider; and gate it all with an offline mock-endpoint
cache guard plus a live before/after benchmark harness.

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: Go 1.25+ (CGO-free builds; `modernc.org/sqlite`)

**Primary Dependencies**: stdlib `net/http` + `encoding/json` (request path), Bubble Tea v2
(TUI), `modernc.org/sqlite` (state); no new third-party dependencies planned

**Storage**: SQLite `state/muhiyacode.sqlite` (sessions/events/trust) + per-session JSON
bundles (`history.json`, `transcript.jsonl`); additive new artifacts: `usage.jsonl` per
session, persisted MCP schema cache, probe snapshot (exact shapes in
[data-model.md](data-model.md))

**Testing**: `go test ./... -count=1` (unit + golden byte-stability + mock-endpoint cache-hit
guard); `CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -race` on Linux/macOS runners; live benchmark harness under
`benchmarks/` (real gateway, excluded from unit runs)

**Target Platform**: Windows / Linux / macOS terminals, amd64 + arm64

**Project Type**: single self-contained CLI/TUI binary

**Performance Goals**: steady-state 99–100% cache-hit rate on cache-eligible tokens from each
session's second request onward (SC-001); zero uncached retransmission of unchanged context in
steady-state turns (SC-003); byte-identical request rebuild across restart/resume (SC-002)

**Constraints**: Constitution v1.0.0 Principles I–X; `~/.muhiya` state layout is a
compatibility boundary (additive changes only); OpenAI-compatible endpoints without cache
support must degrade gracefully (FR-013); system-prompt regression ceiling (~1,900 estimated
tokens) and existing prompt-stability gates must keep passing

**Scale/Scope**: sessions of 20+ turns against 64K–128K-context models; multi-MCP-server
configurations; concurrent subagent traffic; six identified defects (G1–G6) + accounting gaps
across ~10 packages

## Constitution Check

*GATE: evaluated pre-Phase 0 and re-evaluated post-Phase 1 design. Result: PASS (no
violations; no Complexity Tracking entries).*

| Principle | Gate evaluation |
|---|---|
| I. Correctness Before Optimization | PASS — every optimization preserves behavior: pinned MCP surfaces still execute live tools (forwarding), read dedup keeps mtime/size invalidation, date still delivered every task (via brief). Freshness edges (file changes) explicitly protected (FR-012); quality regressions block per SC-006. |
| II. Cache Efficiency Without Quality Loss | PASS — no content the model needs is removed: fold/trim/compact capabilities retained (scheduling changes only), model addenda kept (D11), skills/knowledge behavior untouched. The one deliberate tradeoff — MCP schema freshness deferred one session — is inherited from the reference, documented, and bypassed by explicit user action (D1). |
| III. Deterministic Stable Prefix | PASS — the design's core: date removed from prompt (D2), probe snapshot persisted (D3), MCP block sorted + pinned (D1), golden byte tests + restart determinism tests (D7, D10). |
| IV. Separation of Dynamic and Cached Content | PASS — date joins task brief on the user turn (D2); goal/plan/steering/effort placements already conform (research B3/B4) and gain regression tests. |
| V. No Redundant Retransmission | PASS — rewrite floor 0.60 + boundary scheduling + anti-thrash latch (D4); read dedup preserved; reasoning replay stripped to provider-required minimum (D9). |
| VI. Honest Measurement | PASS — distinct nullable read/miss/output fields from provider payloads only; "unavailable" semantics; persisted per-request records; pressure triggers switch from estimates to provider-reported `prompt_tokens` (D5, D4). |
| VII. Reference Architecture: DeepSeek Reasonix | PASS — full evidence-based analysis with adopt/adapt/reject matrix completed in [research.md](research.md) Parts A/C before design. |
| VIII. Improve, Don't Rewrite | PASS — targeted fixes at defect sites; map-based envelope kept (D10); no subsystem rewrites; the persisted MCP schema cache is a new additive component justified as the reference-proven fix for the top two defects. |
| IX. Clean, Maintainable, Secure, Provider-Compatible | PASS — no new deps; additive state files only; MCP secrets handling untouched; graceful degradation on providers without cache reporting (FR-013). |
| X. Verified Improvements | PASS — offline cache guard (D7) + live before/after harness with pinned config and N≥3 runs (D8); results stored under `specs/001-prompt-cache-optimization/benchmarks/`. |

(`contract` inward) unchanged.

## Implementation Design (workstreams)

Ordered to keep the system shippable after each workstream; W1 is the measurement foundation
required to prove everything else (Principle VI before optimization claims).

### W1 — Honest measurement foundation (FR-007, FR-013; D5)
Extend `contract.Usage` with nullable `CacheReadTokens` / `CacheMissTokens` (distinct from the
legacy single `CachedTokens`, which remains derived for display compatibility); parse both
DeepSeek top-level and OpenAI nested shapes in `sse.go`, deriving miss = prompt − cached only
when the provider gives cached without miss, and marking derived values as derived; append one
usage record per request to `sessions/<id>/usage.jsonl`; restore session aggregates on resume;
surface per-request and session hit rate + read/uncached/output splits in `/context`, the
activity line, and task summaries. Baseline capture (quickstart step 1) happens immediately
after W1 lands, before any behavior change.

### W2 — Deterministic tool surface (FR-001, FR-002, FR-005, FR-006; D1, D3)
MCP schema cache persisted per server-spec fingerprint; session build registers the pinned,
name-sorted, canonicalized-once MCP block before the first request; execution forwards to live
tools; live handshakes refresh only the disk cache; read-only `/mcp` actions never touch the
registry; mutating actions apply at a task boundary and record a `toolset-change` event.
Web-probe snapshot persisted with last-good merge.

### W3 — Stable prompt fields (FR-001, FR-003; D2, D11)
Date out of the prompt template and into the task brief; `/model` triggers a prompt-context
refresh recorded as `model-switch`. Prompt regression ceiling tests updated.

### W4 — Rewrite scheduling (FR-004, FR-005, FR-006; D4)
Pressure floor 0.60 for any rewrite of transmitted bytes; fold+trim consolidated into one
maintenance pass at task/turn boundaries; anti-thrash latch; pressure computed from
provider-reported prompt tokens (estimator as bootstrap only); every pass recorded with cause
and scope; window-drop recorded when it fires. Threshold values tuned against the W6 harness
within the bounds set in D4.

### W5 — Attribution and replay hygiene (FR-005, FR-008; D6, D9)
`PrefixShape` computed per request (system bytes, canonical tool bytes, rewrite version, model
ID); compare-and-record invalidation events; provider-side misses classified when shape is
unchanged; reasoning-content replay verified/conformed to the DeepSeek minimum; retry and
resume paths covered by byte-identity tests.

### W6 — Verification and documentation (FR-009–FR-012; D7, D8, D12)
Mock-endpoint cache guard suite (dialogue, tool loops, MCP-pinned, restart replay, steering,
maintenance scenarios; ≥90% guard threshold); restart determinism test; live `cachebench`
harness (≥20-turn scripted workload, N≥3 runs, JSON output: per-request read/miss/output,
session hit rate, latency, cost); before/after protocol per [quickstart.md](quickstart.md);
`docs/prompt-caching.md` with the limitations register; README/agent-design/architecture
updates where they describe changed behavior (constitution workflow gate).

## Post-Design Constitution Re-Check

Re-evaluated after Phase 1 design artifacts: all ten gates still PASS. The only deliberate
tradeoff (MCP schema freshness deferred one session, D1) is documented in research.md Part C,
carries an explicit user-action bypass, and is the reference-proven pattern the constitution
directs us to study; it does not remove model-visible capability (Principle II satisfied).
